questions.q: Beyond the org-wide 75% average, what additional Apex test coverage requirement does this lesson describe?
options: Every Visualforce page must have its own test class
Every method must be covered by at least 10 separate test methods
Every trigger must have some test coverage of its own, or deployment can be blocked even with a passing org-wide average
Test classes must themselves be covered by other test classes
questions.explain: An org can be above 75% overall and still have a deployment blocked by a single trigger with zero test coverage -- every trigger needs its own coverage.

questions.q: What does `Test.stopTest()` do that matters for testing `WarrantyClaimTriggerHandler.afterInsert`?
options: It forces any asynchronous jobs enqueued inside the startTest/stopTest block, like the Queueable, to run synchronously before returning
It deletes all test data created in the test
It disables governor limits permanently for the org
It prevents the test from running more than once
questions.explain: Test.stopTest() runs enqueued async jobs synchronously before it returns, which is how a test can assert on a Queueable job's results at all.

questions.q: Why does the test class use `@TestSetup` to create an Account, Asset, and Service_Contract__c rather than relying on existing org data?
options: Because @TestSetup is required syntax with no functional purpose
Because Apex tests run in isolation from real org data by default, unless SeeAllData=true is used, which this capstone deliberately avoids
Because Account and Asset records cannot be created in test context
Because Service_Contract__c is a standard object exempt from test isolation
questions.explain: Tests don't see existing org data by default; @TestSetup creates the data the test actually needs, which keeps the test repeatable in any org rather than dependent on data that happens to already exist.

questions.q: Why does the lesson's test suite include a 50-record bulk insert test, rather than only single-record tests?
options: Bulk tests run faster than single-record tests
Salesforce requires at least 50 test records per test class
50 is the maximum number of records Apex can insert at once
A single-record test can't exercise the trigger handler under more than one record per transaction, which the bulk test is designed to do
questions.explain: The bulk test exists to exercise the handler under multiple records in one transaction -- something a test that only inserts one record at a time cannot do. Lesson 20 revisits why passing at this volume still doesn't prove safety at every volume.

questions.q: Why does testing `WarrantyClaimTriggerHandler`'s callout-triggering logic use `HttpCalloutMock` instead of letting the real callout happen?
options: A live network call in every test run would be slow, unreliable, and dependent on a real external system you don't control
Apex tests are physically incapable of compiling any callout code
HttpCalloutMock is required syntax with no functional effect
Mocking is only needed when testing Lightning Web Components, not Apex
questions.explain: Mocking the callout avoids slow, unreliable, uncontrolled dependency on a live external system during every test run, returning a canned response instead.
